summary: Reconcile published Python content with exact source

delivery.outcome: Expose opt-in bounded public-wheel Python-content comparison bound to exact clean Git source, with typed unknown/divergence and a separate reconciliation signal that cannot trigger existing-version reupload.
nonGoals: No source edits, repair, upload or merge authorized by observations
No broad binary/private/multiple registry artifact adapter
No claim of complete artifact/source reproducibility from Python-content comparison
No packaging/version/lock changes; join the already accepted material 2.2.7 integration before its first registry upload

architecture.decision: Extend the shared Goal JSON observer with --verify-source for --project, bounded SHA-256-verified public wheel reads and explicit static setuptools flat/src package matching against immutable clean Git content. Preserve existing version presence, missing-release readiness and publication_verified=false. Source-content divergence exposes reconciliation_required separately, retaining source/head and artifact/manifest evidence; uncertainty and HTTP Retry-After defer. The consumer never compares artifacts itself.
architecture.rollback: Protected revert of this opt-in comparison; retain all existing registry observation and publication checks.

commands: Goal publishes accepted 2.2.7 from clean merged source
Verify both registry artifacts against Git and installed pip-less/source-divergence canaries
